questions.question: What signs did Seeta offer Hanumaan as proof of their meeting? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Seeta gave Hanuman her jewel (choodamani) and narrated incidents known only to
  • Rama and herself, such as how he broke the bow at her swayamvara. These personal
  • tokens and recollections served as proof of their meeting. [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Compare how shame is portrayed in the headmaster in Pothichoru and Vellayi-appan in After the Hanging. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• The headmaster’s shame is internal and moral—stemming from his awareness of
  • personal inadequacy and societal judgment. Vellayi-appan’s shame is existential—
  • rooted in helplessness before fate and injustice. Both reflect how shame functions as
  • an inner mirror of conscience shaped by social and emotional codes. [CO2]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does tinai reflect the harmony between environment and human experience? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Tinai (landscape ecology in Sangam literature) represents the deep interconnection
  • between land, mood, and life. Each tinai corresponds to specific emotions and human
  • activities (love, valour, grief), showing how environment and humanity co-exist
  • harmoniously. [CO3]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the role of moral counsel as represented by Kripacharya's pleas. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Kripacharya symbolises the voice of dharma and restraint amidst chaos. His counsel
  • to Aswatthama before the night slaughter illustrates the enduring struggle between
  • righteousness and vengeance in the Mahabharata. He upholds the moral law even
  • when others abandon it. [CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the role of family in "Sweet Pudding" and community in "Biriyani", and how food reflects both contexts. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• In Sweet Pudding, food signifies domestic bonding and care amid poverty and
  • emotional distance. In Biriyani, it becomes a marker of identity, culture, and
  • communal sharing, symbolising social belonging. Both use food as emotional and
  • cultural language connecting personal and social spaces. [CO2]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: List the sounds of nature that appear in What She Said. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:

  • and the whisper of the wind—all merging human emotion with the rhythms of nature.

questions.question: Examine how children’s innocence functions as a contrast to adult grief in both stories "After the Hanging" and "Sweet Pudding". / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Children’s innocence provides hope and purity against the backdrop of despair and
  • injustice. In both stories, their naive actions mirror the world’s lost morality, offering
  • a spiritual redemption to adult suffering. [CO2]

questions.question: What tone dominates in the poem What the Servants Said? / [CO3] [8x5 = 40]
questions.solution_html:
• The dominant tone is ironic compassion. Through the servants’ simple speech, the
  • poem reflects empathy, satire, and the subtle dignity of the marginalised. [CO3]
